competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample only compares two already-stated lengths for equality (e.g. seed 42's 'Segment A is 21 cm long. Segment B is 21 cm long. Are Segment A and Segment B equal in length?'); no sample involves reading a ruler or performing a draw/construct action, so the competency's 'using a ruler' tool-use is never tested.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both equal-length ('Yes') and unequal-length ('No') cases are represented, and both cm and m units appear (seed 604's '2 m').

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Segment lengths reach 409 cm (seed 500), 328 cm (seed 501), and 259 cm (seed 502) — well beyond what a Grade 3 student could practically measure or draw with a classroom ruler, undermining the 'using a ruler' framing of the competency.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every sample follows the identical structure seen in seed 42, 'Segment A is 21 cm long. Segment B is 21 cm long. Are Segment A and Segment B equal in length?', just with different lengths; there is no ruler-reading or drawing-based variant.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty varies only by the numeric length values compared, not by the specific ruler-use or drawing skill the competency names.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Lengths as large as 409 cm (seed 500: 'Segment A is 409 cm long. Segment B is 409 cm long.') are unrealistic for a hands-on ruler-measurement exercise, since a standard classroom ruler measures well under 100 cm.
